resharding.duplication_note: every replicated tensor is written once per shard, and the tied embedding is stored under both wte.weight and lm_head.weight, so the four shards come to more than four times a quarter of the model. Deduplicating replicated tensors to rank 0 is not implemented.

async_checkpoint.note: the blocking figure is what the training step pays. The async arm blocks for a host-memory copy of the state and nothing else; the write happens on a background thread. The ratio moves a lot between runs because the synchronous arm is at the mercy of the page cache.

streaming.ceiling_note: the ceiling is 2.00x when a read and a step cost the same, because perfect overlap halves the total. Against a page-cached memmap the reader thread is pure overhead and prefetch is a loss.

failure_restart.recovery_note: time to recover here is almost entirely process startup and importing torch. On a real job the same interval also contains the scheduler noticing, requeueing, allocating replacement nodes and re-reading a checkpoint of hundreds of gigabytes over the storage fabric.

collectives.transport: loopback TCP on this machine, not a fabric
collectives.note: the fitted constants move with the machine's load; R^2 is the claim. Below about 64 KiB a gloo all-reduce is latency and scheduling noise and no affine model describes it, which is the model's own point.

fabric_model.status: MODELLED from published peak bandwidths, not measured

nvlink4.source: NVIDIA H100 datasheet: 18 NVLink 4 links x 25 GB/s per direction = 900 GB/s bidirectional aggregate per GPU; NVSwitch gives every GPU in the 8-GPU node that bandwidth all-to-all.

nvlink3.source: NVIDIA A100 datasheet: 12 NVLink 3 links x 25 GB/s per direction = 600 GB/s bidirectional aggregate per GPU.

pcie5.source: PCI-SIG: Gen5 is 32 GT/s per lane, 128b/130b encoded; x16 is ~63 GB/s per direction. This is the ceiling for a PCIe-attached GPU with no NVLink.

ib_ndr.source: NVIDIA DGX H100: 8 x ConnectX-7 NDR400 compute NICs, 400 Gb/s = 50 GB/s each, one per GPU, so 50 GB/s per GPU and 400 GB/s per node.

ib_hdr.source: NVIDIA DGX A100: 8 x HDR200 compute NICs, 200 Gb/s = 25 GB/s each.

roce200.source: 200 GbE line rate = 25 GB/s. RoCE v2 puts the same RDMA verbs on Ethernet; the wire rate matches HDR but it needs a lossless fabric (PFC/ECN) to get near it, and its small-message latency is higher.

meta.measured_vs_modelled: resharding, async_checkpoint, streaming, failure_restart and collectives are MEASURED on this machine. fabric_model is MODELLED from the published bandwidths it carries with it.
